# Infinite vs Parcha (now Grep AI) for compliance work


Parcha (parcha.ai) built AI agents that ran KYB, KYC, and enhanced due diligence research for fintech compliance teams. As of September 14, 2026, its site announces that Parcha is now Grep AI and that the original product line was retired in favor of a general platform for research-intensive knowledge work.[Infinite](https://infinite.net/) went the other direction: a network that runs its own compliance program, with Compliance AI built for that work alone.


By[Nikhil Srinivasan](https://infinite.net/company/about) , Founder & CEO


·


Last updated Sep 14, 2026

TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Parcha's compliance agents (KYB, KYC, EDD) were point agents: deep research delivered as reports and exports into a workflow the customer still owned.
2. Parcha now operates as Grep AI, a platform for research-intensive knowledge work; its site says the original product line was retired.
3. A research agent makes the analyst's file richer; it does not change who runs the program, procures the providers, or answers the examiner.
4. Compliance AI is built for compliance casework alone and runs Infinite's own program today, with a named analyst signing every decision.
5. On Infinite, research done once travels: a counterparty cleared on the network is cleared for every business on it.


01


## What Parcha built


Parcha's product pages, still live as of September 14, 2026, describe one agent per check type. A KYB agent unified legal-status verification, ownership identification down to beneficial owners, sanctions screening, and adverse-media review into a single workflow. An enhanced due diligence agent extended the same approach to high-risk entities. The output was a documented file: "All Parcha results include comprehensive audit trails with source documentation, confidence scores, and detailed rationale," exportable as PDFs and CSVs. The customer stayed in charge of the workflow: "You are always in control of how AI is used to carry out each step in your compliance workflow."


That was good research automation, and the source-traced output was a genuine strength. It was also, by design, a point agent: it made one step in a compliance program faster and handed the result back into a case system, a policy, a provider stack, and a review process the customer still ran.


02


## What changed: Parcha is now Grep AI


The parcha.ai home page now reads, verbatim: "Parcha is now Grep AI. We retired Parcha's original product line to focus on Grep AI, a new platform for automating research-intensive, high-stakes knowledge work with AI agents." The same page tells its banking and fintech customers that "our commitment to accelerating compliance workflows hasn't changed" and that Grep agents "are already automating compliance work across multiple global fintechs and banks."


Grep's site describes a harness that routes each step of a task to the model best suited to it, frontier or open-source, with built-in research skills, maintained data integrations, and results that trace back to their sources. Read neutrally, this is a horizontal research platform in which compliance is one application among many, configured by the customer's team. That is a legitimate product. For a compliance buyer it changes the question: you are no longer choosing a compliance vendor, you are choosing a general research platform and building the compliance use case on it yourself.


03


## The point-agent pattern, and its limit


A research agent improves the research. It does not touch the rest of the program: the case system where the file lands, the identity, screening, and monitoring providers that still have to be procured and integrated, the written policy, the quality control, the exam. And its work does not compound. The same legal entity researched today for one fintech will be researched again next month for the next one, by a different agent, from scratch, because the result lives in one customer's file.


> A better research agent gives the analyst a better file. A network gives the next analyst a file that is already done.


04


## Where Infinite differs


[Compliance AI](https://infinite.net/compliance/ai) is built for compliance casework and nothing else, and it runs Infinite's own compliance program today: onboarding reviews, transaction-monitoring dispositions, and case assembly across the network. Its agents operate the real tools of the work (screening, document verification, device intelligence, ledger history, the case file itself) and draw on the context of the account graph, so no review starts cold. Every decision routes to a named analyst through a gate that cannot be configured away, and every step is logged and exportable.


The word "harness" appears in both companies' vocabulary and means different things. At Grep it is the layer that routes work to the best model per step. On Infinite the harness is the accountability layer: the tools the agents are allowed to operate, the gates they must route through, and the record they leave behind. Model choice is a component inside that harness, never the guarantee, so nothing about the exam posture changes when a model does.


And because the program runs on a network, the work compounds. A business vetted once on Infinite is vetted for every business on it; first-time counterparty reviews that take around 30 days under one-off manual review close in 1–2 days. Onboarding reaches your customers through[hosted flows that carry your brand](https://infinite.net/compliance/embedded) , with review states and information requests you can query.


05


## When each fits


If the job is research automation across many domains, run by a team that wants to configure its own workflow on a general platform, Grep is built for that. If the job is compliance casework on a live money product, with a program someone runs end to end and results that carry across the network, that is the job Infinite is built for. For how the other case management AI models compare, see[case management AI: five models compared](https://infinite.net/learn/insights/case-management-ai) .


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Is Parcha still a compliance product?


As of September 14, 2026, parcha.ai states that Parcha is now Grep AI and that Parcha's original product line was retired in favor of a general platform for research-intensive knowledge work. The same page says Grep agents continue to automate compliance work for fintechs and banks, so compliance is now one use case of a broader platform rather than the product.


### How is Infinite different from Parcha or Grep AI?


Grep AI is a research-agent platform a team configures for its own workflow; the program, providers, case system, and exam stay with the customer. Infinite runs its own compliance program on a network, with Compliance AI built for that casework: agents assemble the case, a named analyst signs, and a counterparty cleared once is cleared for every business on the network.


### Can AI agents run KYB and EDD research without a human decision?


The research, yes; the decision, no. Agents can assemble registry data, ownership, screening hits, and adverse media into a documented file. On Infinite the disposition is always[made and signed by a named analyst](https://infinite.net/compliance/ai) ; there is no configuration in which the AI approves, rejects, or closes a case.
